clue.text: Copper isn't very well behaved

parts.note: a cheap metal falls short of the precious yellow one in value, while the idiom for a child who behaves perfectly compares them to that precious metal

explanation.surface: A grumble that a policeman is not behaving himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like slang for a police officer, but here it is the metal, which is not worth as much as gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a perfectly behaved child, usually praised by a parent or teacher.

clue.text: Party with blonde when weather forecast's favourable

parts.note: a set is a group of people who socialise together, like a party
fair hair is light-coloured or blonde

explanation.surface: A party that includes a blonde guest, held when the weather looks good.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the barometer reading for settled, sunny weather, the good outlook a forecaster gives.

clue.text: Developing vegetables for gardeners

parts.note: small immature bulbs that gardeners plant out to grow into full-sized alliums

explanation.surface: Vegetables still growing, meant for keen gardeners.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tiny bulbs grown for one season and planted the next, which then develop into mature vegetables.

clue.text: The prosecutor has to act — see foot of column

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, the American public prosecutor
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: The prosecutor must act, and the instruction points to a footnote at the bottom of the newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot of column' looks like a newspaper cross-reference, but it is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this is the cube-shaped part of a pedestal, the base on which a column stands.

clue.text: Fairy tales will give security for children, say

indicators.note: the letters of the two story words will give, once rearranged, a new phrase

explanation.surface: Bedtime stories make children feel secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will give' signals that the letters of FAIRY TALES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard bar fitted beside beds or stairs keeps youngsters from falling, an example of protection for them.

clue.text: A possessive type

parts.note: sounds like a jealous person, but means simply someone who possesses something

explanation.surface: A description of a clingy, jealous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessive' suggests jealousy; here it just means having possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding title to property is literally the person who possesses it.

clue.text: Lengthen transvestite apparel no longer in fashion?

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex, worn by drag performers
out means unfashionable, the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A question about letting out cross-dressing outfits that have gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to make it last longer than necessary, as with a dull meeting.

clue.text: Ruth upset after ruining the joyful holiday abroad

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled name at the end of the rearranged phrase
ruining wrecks the order of the three words before it, so they are rearranged
upset knocks the name's letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Ruth is upset because something spoiled a happy holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' is fair because this is the American Independence Day, a foreign holiday to a British solver; 'after' places the shuffled name last.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence Day is the American national holiday, so foreign from a British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Narrowly failed, received a school caning

definitions.meaning: lost a race by the tiniest margin, the length of a horse's skull
punished by the headteacher with a cane, read literally

explanation.surface: A pupil who just missed out, and was caned at school as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The racing phrase means losing by a very small margin; read literally, it means thrashed by a headmaster.

clue.text: Lacking Test experience, I run Ted out

indicators.note: out signals the three words are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer with no Test caps runs out his partner Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; being 'run out' is a way of losing your wicket in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never put to the test has not been tried yet, a newcomer without proven experience.

clue.text: An enthusiast to get on and flourish

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or enthusiast
to fare is to get on or manage, as in how did you fare

explanation.surface: An enthusiast getting on well and thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' looks like a verb meaning thrive; it is a noun, a showy burst of trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet call heralding an arrival is a musical flourish.

clue.text: Long to reach agreement on service

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, an agreement in a vote
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A wish to reach agreement on terms of service.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it.

clue.text: Renowned solicitor to open proceedings

parts.note: star used as an adjective means famous or celebrated, as in a star player
a tout solicits custom, for instance selling tickets

explanation.surface: A famous lawyer opens a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin is to set off or commence, opening the action.

clue.text: A powerful grip, useful in defence

parts.note: strong means powerful or mighty
a hold is a grip or grasp

explanation.surface: A firm grasp that helps a defender, as in wrestling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or castle is a fortified place held against attack, so it serves the defence.

clue.text: The more they cut down the more they gain

definitions.text: The more they cut down the more they gain

parts.words: The more they cut down the more they gain
parts.note: sounds like a paradox about savings; really describes reapers cutting crops and gathering grain

explanation.surface: A paradox about people who profit by cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' suggests economising; here it means cutting crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Reapers and combines bring in crops by cutting them, so more cutting means a larger yield.

clue.text: Shock caused by teachers union retraction

indicators.note: a retraction draws something back, so the union's letters run backwards

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers; read as the possessive NUT's, the S comes with it

explanation.surface: A teachers' union withdraws a statement, to general shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was a British teachers' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or stupefy someone is to give them a shock.

clue.text: Lock controller

parts.note: sounds like a canal lock keeper; a lock is also a tress of hair held in place by a clip

explanation.surface: Someone who operates a canal lock or a security lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a canal or door; here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sprung clip keeps a lock of hair in place.

clue.text: Standard laid down for pavements

definitions.meaning: a banner or ensign, as in the royal standard
a flat paving stone, a flagstone

explanation.surface: A standard set down for paving.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a standard, and a flagstone is a slab laid on pavements.

clue.text: Bar and a club

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A pub with a bar and a club attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a metal bar in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is a metal support, one of a pair of bars holding logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Workers' reward for doing nothing?

parts.note: sounds like a complaint about idle staff; really the wages paid while employees are on leave

explanation.surface: A jibe that staff get paid for idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Employees on annual leave still receive wages, money earned while not working.

clue.text: Game of bridge?

definitions.meaning: a card game, the British name for blackjack or twenty-one
a floating bridge supported on boats or floats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game of bridge' suggests the card game bridge, but the answer is a different card game and also a kind of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a card game like blackjack and a temporary floating bridge.

clue.text: Legally only of minor importance

parts.note: sounds trivial in law, but means a minor in law, too young

explanation.surface: A legal matter being dismissed as trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor importance' suggests triviality; a minor is a person below adult age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone below the legal age of adulthood is a minor in law.

clue.text: True capital of Moroccan kingdom

parts.note: real means genuine or true

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, its upper-case initial

explanation.surface: A query about the true capital of Morocco's kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' looks like a city, but means the first letter of Moroccan.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Managed to get central heating at the farm

parts.note: ran means managed or ran the business
CH is the standard abbreviation for central heating, in house adverts

explanation.surface: Someone managed to install central heating on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large American cattle farm is called this, so it is a type of farm.

clue.text: Put out — nothing is fit for the job

indicators.note: out says the three letters are put out of order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed that nothing is up to the task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like 'annoyed'; 'out' rearranges PUT into UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable of a task is being equal to it, as in he is not up to it.

clue.text: Rent-a-party? It's a wind-up

parts.note: rent is the past participle of rend, meaning torn
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A rent-a-party firm turns out to be a hoax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like hiring; here it means torn. 'wind-up' looks like a prank but describes a spiralling wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating column of air, a wind that whirls upward.

clue.text: Walk between the plants

parts.note: sounds like strolling in a garden; describes an arched framework covered with climbers over a path

explanation.surface: A stroll through the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden structure is a covered walkway with climbing plants trained over its trellis.

clue.text: Celebrity parachuting in attempt to impress

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity
parachuting means dropping from an aircraft

explanation.surface: A celebrity parachutes in to impress people.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances is a way to try to impress others.
